ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: On a certain island lives a kind of animal whose population size has remained relatively stable for many years. Individuals of this animal need 6 months from birth to sexual maturity. The figure shows the age structure of this animal population in different months of a certain year (the number of individuals in each age group of the population is counted on the last day of each month). Please answer: could the birth rate of this population in October be 0?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the figure is an age-structure bar chart of this animal in February, April, June, August, October, and December; the vertical axis is individual percentage, and the legend distinguishes immature individuals, mature individuals, and senescent individuals. In the bar chart corresponding to October, a certain proportion of immature individuals can still be seen. Then reason: the question stem states that this animal needs 6 months from birth to sexual maturity, and that the data for each month are counted on the last day of the month. The immature individuals counted at the end of October can only indicate that these individuals have not yet reached 6 months after birth, and they are not necessarily individuals born in October. If no new individuals were born in October, the immature individuals at the end of October could still be individuals born from May to September. Therefore, the birth rate in October could be 0.
